sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.8% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, reaching $31.7 billion [F198][F9].
Operating income grew faster, at 5.8% a year, lifting operating margin from 22.9% to 27.2% [F199][F20][F28].
FY2022 was the step change in the top line, with revenue up 17.1% on rate cases, favorable weather and volumes [D239][P26].
FY2020 was the trough, when net income fell 63.3% on coal ash settlement impairments and pandemic-driven volume losses [D157][P60].
Electric Utilities and Infrastructure supplied 90.9% of FY2025 revenue and added 3.6pp of the 5.6% growth [D541][D543][D358].
Residential electric was the largest customer class at 43.3% of revenue, contributing 2.8pp in FY2025 [D774][D776].
Gas Utilities and Infrastructure grew 27.1% in FY2025, adding 2.0pp, with Piedmont Natural Gas up 32.1% [D565][D566][D682].
Operating income grew 8.8% against 5.6% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 41.4% [D359][D358][D378].
Diluted EPS rose 10.5% in FY2025, ahead of 9.8% net income growth, despite a 0.6% larger share count [D362][D360][D374].
FY2025 operating margin of 27.2% is the window high, 4.3pp above the 22.9% median and 7.5pp above the FY2020 low [F28][D932][D933][D931].
The FY2025 margin widened 0.8pp as revenue growth outpaced operating-cost growth by only 0.3pp [D370][D379].
D&A rose to 24.3% of revenue from 21.4%, a 2.9pp drag that other cost lines offset [D341][D303].
Net margin of 15.7% sits 11.5pp below operating margin, reflecting interest expense of $3.6 billion and a 11.2% tax rate [F47][D967][X63][D345].
Net margin ranks in the 25th percentile against utilities peers, whose median is 17.6% [D951][D952].
Operating cash flow of $12.3 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, near the 2.59x window median [F77][D346][D958].
Capex of $14.0 billion, 44.2% of revenue and 1.82x D&A, pushed free cash flow to -$1.7 billion, a -5.3% margin [F87][D342][D348][F97][D343].
FY2022 conversion fell to 2.32x as rising fuel costs created undercollections that increased borrowings [D226][P36].
Stock-based compensation is immaterial at 0.8% of operating cash flow [D349].
Net debt reached $89.6 billion in FY2025, up from $50.0 billion in FY2016, as total debt rose 6.6% [D352][D14][D376].
Net debt is 282.3% of revenue, in the 33rd percentile of three utilities peers, against a peer median net cash position of -235.4% of revenue [D353][D968][D969].
Cash of $245 million covers 0.1 years of the latest burn, and the current ratio fell to 0.55x [D350][D356][F177].
Dividends of $3.2 billion in FY2022 exceeded free cash flow, and the diluted share count rose 4.2% in FY2021 [D234][F94][D214].
The current ratio of 0.55x is below 1.0x and near the 0.53x window low, leaving little liquidity cushion [F177][D943].
Net debt has risen nine straight years to $89.6 billion, funding a capex programme that keeps free cash flow negative [D352][R3][F97].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, at -0.96x, 0.01x and -0.34x [D269][D309][D347][R4].
FY2021 operating expenses, pretax income and tax were later restated, so that year's margin comparisons carry a data-quality caveat [X29][X69][X79][R6][R7][R8].
If operating margin holds above the 27.2% FY2025 high, the cost discipline of FY2024-FY2025 is confirmed; a drop toward the 22.9% median would reverse it [F28][D932][D933].
Free cash flow margin above the -5.8% median would signal capex is peaking; a repeat of the -19.0% FY2022 low would deepen the funding gap [D939][D937].
Net debt above $89.6 billion in the next 10-K would extend the nine-year climb; a decline would break it [D352][R3].
